name: Halmstad
title: Ship Thickness Measurement in Halmstad | Bulk, Steel and Paper
description: Thickness measurement in Halmstad for bulk carriers, general cargo ships and feeders carrying steel, scrap and paper: hold, tank-top, ballast tank and deck UTM.
h1: UTM and Hull Gauging for Cargo Ships at the Port of Halmstad
intro: Halmstad grew up where the River Nissan reaches the Kattegat, and its port, run together with Varberg by Hallands Hamnar, now handles a broad mix: forest products and paper, steel, recycled metal, containers, bulk cargo and fuels. That variety brings general cargo ships, small bulkers and feeders, each with its own pattern of wear in holds and tanks. No one from Atlantis is stationed in Halmstad; a team travels from India to each ship and works alongside under arrangements made by the agent.

highlights.p: Recycled metal is loaded by grab and magnet, and steel products bear down on tank tops in concentrated loads. Both leave tank tops, hopper plating and lower frames dented, scored and thinned, so hold gauging after discharge is a common request from owners of ships in these trades.

Oceanhamnen, the newest part of the port, has a 200-metre quay with a draught of twelve metres, which lets larger bulk and general cargo ships call. Those ships often stay alongside for a full working day or more, which suits a broader gauging scope.

Paper and other forest products have to travel dry and clean. Wasted hatch coamings, leaking cover joints and rusting hold steel all risk cargo claims, so owners in the paper trade ask for hatch, coaming and hold readings well before a problem shows up at discharge.

port.h: The Port of Halmstad: a mixed cargo port at the mouth of the Nissan
p: Halmstad lies on the southern part of the Halland coast, facing the Kattegat across open water, with Denmark's Jutland coast well beyond the horizon. The older quays grew up near the mouth of the River Nissan, close to the town centre, while newer and deeper berths have been built further out towards the sea, where ships have more room to manoeuvre and lorries and trains have more space to work. The approach from the Kattegat is direct, without the island passages of the Bohuslän or Blekinge coasts, and the harbour is generally free of ice. Ports of Halland, formed in 2012 when the Varberg and Halmstad ports were brought under one company, runs the port today and has been investing in its quays and in charging infrastructure as part of a wider electrification effort.

The cargo base is broad for a port of its size. Forest products and paper move through Halmstad alongside steel, recycled metal, containers, bulk cargo and fuels, often on the same day and at neighbouring berths. The ships that come are correspondingly varied: general cargo and multipurpose ships carrying steel and forest products, small bulk carriers loading scrap and other dry bulk, container feeders connecting with larger hubs, and coastal tankers bringing in fuel. Most are short-sea vessels trading around the North Sea and Baltic, owned and managed from across northern Europe, and many call regularly enough for their superintendents to plan inspection work around a known Halmstad visit. Some carry one cargo in and another out, discharging steel or fuel and then loading forest products or scrap, which can leave a hold empty for a few hours between the two.

Each cargo leaves its mark on the ships that carry it. Scrap is the harshest: heavy pieces are dropped into the hold, grabs and magnets strike tank tops and hopper plates, and the cargo itself can hold moisture and residues that eat into the steel. Steel coils and plates bear on narrow areas of the tank top, and paper reels demand dry, clean holds with tight hatches. So the gauging requested here is mostly about holds, tank tops, hopper and topside tanks and hatch coamings, with ballast tanks and deck plating added when a survey is due. The port's mix also means it is a convenient place for owners to check ships that have changed trades, for example from scrap to forest products, and want the condition of the holds documented before the first cargo of the new trade.

facilities.h: Where ships are gauged in Halmstad
p: Halmstad is a cargo port rather than a repair centre, so gauging is done with the ship afloat at her loading or discharge berth, or at a lay-by quay if she is waiting for cargo. Holds are reached most easily once discharge is complete and the hold has been swept, or before loading starts if the ship arrives empty. Hatch covers and coamings are measured while the covers are open and the hatch is not being worked. Ballast tanks need to be emptied, ventilated and certified safe for entry by the crew, so they are scheduled when the ship's ballast plan allows it, usually agreed with the chief officer before arrival.

For docking, owners send their ships to yards in Denmark, Poland, Germany, the Baltic states or wherever their usual arrangement lies. A Halmstad call before the docking gives the chance to measure holds that are about to be repaired and to send the yard a steel list based on current readings. Varberg is a short distance up the coast and is operated by the same port company, so a team in Halmstad can also attend a ship there on the same trip.
list: Oceanhamnen deep-water quay — broader hold, tank-top and ballast tank gauging on larger bulk and general cargo ships during longer calls.
Quays near the Nissan mouth — hatch coaming, hold and deck readings on general cargo ships loading or discharging forest products and steel.
Bulk and scrap berths — tank-top, hopper and lower-frame gauging after discharge, with damage mapping where grabs and magnets have struck.
Container berth — ballast tank, deck and scrubber line measurements on feeder ships within the berth window.
Fuel and liquid berths — deck and ballast tank work on coastal tankers, subject to terminal rules and the ship's permit.
Lay-by quays — owner's condition and pre-purchase gauging on ships waiting for cargo or between charters.

context.h: Inspection, regulation and cargo-driven wear in Halmstad
p: The Swedish Transport Agency carries out port state control in Halmstad under the Paris MoU. General cargo ships and older small bulkers form a large part of the traffic, and structural deficiencies on such ships typically centre on hatch covers, coamings, corroded deck fittings and hold structure, which are exactly the areas gauging addresses. Bulk carriers come under the Enhanced Survey Programme, and single-side-skin bulk carriers have specific IACS renewal criteria for hold frames, so a bulker in the scrap trade can reach the point where frames need renewal sooner than her age would suggest.

Two further EU requirements affect the ships here. Ships of 500 gross tonnage and above calling at Halmstad must carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, and larger ships of 5,000 gross tonnage and above report their emissions under the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime. Commercially, paper and steel shippers and their insurers look closely at cargo-handling condition: a hold with heavy scale, damaged coating or leaking hatch joints can lead to rejected cargo or claims. That makes documented hold and hatch condition valuable to owners trading here, alongside the readings their class survey requires.

jobs.h: Thickness measurement jobs typical of Halmstad
jobs.p: The jobs in Halmstad follow the cargo. Scrap and steel ships need their holds checked after hard use; paper and forest-product ships need sound hatches and dry holds; feeders and tankers need ballast tank and deck readings fitted into short calls. We agree each scope with the superintendent before the team travels, confirm with the agent which berth the ship will use and how long she is expected to stay, and arrange the order of work so that measurements in a hold are complete before cargo operations reach it. Reports go to the superintendent the same day, so repair decisions can be taken before the ship sails. Examples include:
list: Tank-top, hopper and lower hold-frame gauging on a bulk carrier after discharging scrap, with grab damage marked for the owner's repair list.
Hatch coaming and cover plate readings on a general cargo ship about to enter the paper trade, documenting condition before the first cargo.
Ballast tank and deck gauging at Oceanhamnen on a larger bulk carrier approaching an intermediate survey.
Pre-purchase hold and tank gauging on a small multipurpose ship lying at a lay-by quay, for a buyer in another country.
Scrubber wash-water line measurements on a container feeder during its regular Halmstad call.

logistics: Halmstad Airport has domestic flights, but the team normally arrives through Copenhagen Airport or Göteborg Landvetter and continues to Halmstad by train on the West Coast Line or by road. The cargo quays are ISPS-controlled, so the ship's agent arranges gate passes for the named technicians and confirms the berth and working hours with the terminal. The team travels from India on Schengen visas, and for ships with regular Halmstad calls a visa obtained once can cover several jobs within its validity.
vessels: Coasters in the steel and scrap trades

faqs.q: Can a ship's holds be gauged straight after discharging scrap in Halmstad?
faqs.a: Yes, once the hold has been swept and residues removed, because readings need clean steel at each measuring point. Tank tops, hopper plating and lower frames are the focus, and grab or magnet damage is recorded alongside the thickness readings. If the ship is loading another cargo straight away, we agree with the chief officer which holds are released to us first.

faqs.q: What should owners in the paper trade have measured?
faqs.a: Hatch cover top plates and side plating, coaming plates and top bars, and the hold structure where rust scale and coating damage could spoil cargo. Readings show whether wastage has reached the point where the steel should be renewed rather than patched. Combining this with the class survey schedule means repairs can be planned for the next docking rather than done in a hurry.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Halmstad?
faqs.a: Halmstad is a cargo port and not a ship-repair centre, so owners dock their ships elsewhere, usually in Denmark, Poland, Germany or the Baltic states. A Halmstad call before the docking is a useful chance to measure holds and tanks and pass the yard a steel list based on current readings, and our team can travel to the yard for the rest of the programme.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover ships in both Halmstad and Varberg?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The two ports are a short distance apart on the same coast and are operated by the same company, so if ships are in both at around the same time, the team can attend them one after the other. We ask for both ships' expected dates early so the visa period and travel plan cover the whole trip.
